prompt_text: I need a personal injury lawyer in Dallas after a truck accident. Which specific law firms should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Dallas for a truck accident case?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — and I can give specific firms you can call right now — but first a quick question: do you need a firm located inside Dallas city limits, or are you OK with large Texas firms who handle Dallas cases? Also: how badly injured were you (minor injuries vs. catastrophic/life-changing)? That will help me tailor recommendations.

If you want names immediately, call these firms — each is known for representing people hurt in commercial truck crashes and for having the resources to investigate big trucking cases:

- Arnold & Itkin (handles catastrophic truck cases statewide)
  - Why call: Nationally known plaintiffs’ trial firm that routinely handles commercial-truck and catastrophic-injury claims. They have experience hiring crash reconstruction experts, dealing with trucking companies/insurers, and litigating large cases.

- Waters & Kraus (Dallas)
  - Why call: Dallas plaintiffs’ firm with experience in catastrophic personal-injury claims. Local presence means familiarity with Dallas courts, judges, and local experts.

- Mark Lanier Law Firm (Texas trial firm)
  - Why call: High-profile trial attorneys who handle complex, high-exposure motor-vehicle and trucking cases and have the trial resources needed for big claims.

- The Law Offices of Jim Adler (“The Texas Hammer”)
  - Why call: Large Texas-focused practice with experience in auto and truck accidents and broad advertising presence—easy to reach for a quick consult and to start immediate claims work.

How to pick which to call first
- Prioritize firms that: (1) regularly handle commercial trucking cases, (2) have trial experience and resources (reconstructionists, life-care planners), and (3) show documented results or peer ratings. 
- Call 3–4 firms and compare: how quickly they’ll investigate, whether they’ll take your case on contingency, who directly handles the file (partner vs. junior associate), and whether they’re willing to go to trial.

What to ask on the initial call (script)
- “Do you handle commercial truck accident cases in Dallas?”  
- “Do you take these on contingency?”  
- “Have you tried truck cases to verdict?”  
- “Will you investigate the crash (black box, logbooks, driver’s record, company safety files)?”  
- “What is your typical fee and costs policy?”  
- “Can you provide a past client reference or recent results for truck cases?”  

Immediate practical steps
- Preserve evidence: photos, videos, medical records, hospital paperwork, police report, truck company/driver info, any dashcam footage.  
- Don’t give recorded statements to the trucking company’s insurer without counsel.  
- Note deadlines: Texas has a two-year statute of limitations for most personal injury suits (exceptions exist). Contact a lawyer quickly.

If you want, tell me your Dallas ZIP or the severity of injuries and I’ll give a 5–7 firm shortlist that’s better-tailored (including boutique Dallas firms and local AV-rated attorneys), plus a ready-to-use phone script you can read on each call.
